Console table for a print method

Source: R/utils_print.R
pr_table.Rd

Print a data frame as an aligned plain-text table: a bold header, a grey rule, then one line per row. Columns are aligned by display width, so Chinese text lines up; P-value columns are coloured by significance, and chosen rows can be highlighted.

Usage

pr_table(
  data,
  p_col = NULL,
  highlight = NULL,
  rownames = FALSE,
  n = 20,
  align = NULL,
  digits = 2,
  width = NULL,
  indent = 2
)

Arguments

data

A data frame (tibbles included).

p_col

Character. Names of the P-value columns, or NULL.

highlight

Rows to highlight in black on light yellow: integer row numbers or a logical vector. Highlighted rows drop their other colours. Missing, fractional and non-finite selectors are rejected; zero and positions outside the displayed rows are ignored.

rownames

Logical. Show the row names as a first, unnamed column, e.g. the terms of as.data.frame(coef(summary(fit))), which are otherwise not shown (default FALSE). Displayed row names are never treated as P values. They can be shown even when there are no value columns.

n

Non-negative integer. Rows to show (default 20); the rest are counted in a grey footer. NULL or Inf shows every row.

align

Column alignment, recycled: "left", "right" or "center". NULL (default) right-aligns numeric and P-value columns and left-aligns the rest.

digits

Integer from 0 to 324. Decimals for double columns (default 2).

width

Positive integer. Line width the table must fit; NULL (default) uses the console width. The first column and the P-value columns always show. Long required headings and, when necessary, cells are cut with an ellipsis; the other columns follow while they fit, and the footer names those left out.

indent

Non-negative integer. Spaces before each line (default 2). Uncoloured highlighted output reserves at least two columns, including its marker, even when a smaller indent is requested.

Value

The printed lines, invisibly.

Details

Cells are formatted as follows. P-value columns: numbers take the stat_pval(mode = "pvalue") wording ("<0.001"), a number just under 0.05 or 0.01 that this wording would round up to the cut-off taking the decimals it needs (0.0499, not 0.050), text is kept as written, and values print bold red below 0.001, red below 0.05 and grey otherwise. Text bounds receive significance styling only when their comparison guarantees a value below the cut-off; lower bounds and invalid numeric text receive none. Decimal text is compared without rounding its endpoint to double precision. Other double columns are rounded to digits decimals, or none when every value is whole; a column whose smallest non-zero value would round to zero gets enough decimals for two significant digits, at most six. Nonzero values still rounded to zero, and numbers wider than the available line, use scientific notation. Missing values print as a grey NA; an explicit missing factor level displays as <NA>. Matrix and array columns are described one row at a time, retaining all components. Packed data-frame columns show each row as a named list. List-column cells are described as in pr_tree(), e.g. <dbl 2> 1.1, 2.2. Everything else uses as.character(). Classed numeric and time-span columns use their format methods, retaining integer64 digits and time units. The optional packages bit64, haven and lubridate are loaded by namespace when their stored types are encountered. POSIXlt date-times display as equivalent POSIXct vectors. Layout control characters in cells and column names are escaped so they cannot introduce extra table rows or misalign columns. A missing column name is displayed as <NA>. Without colour (knitted documents, log files), P values carry stars (*** below 0.001, ** below 0.01, * below 0.05), highlighted rows start with > and missing text cells read <NA>.

See also

Other print helpers: pr_badge(), pr_box(), pr_head(), pr_kv(), pr_note(), pr_section(), pr_spark(), pr_tree()

Examples

res <- data.frame(
  Variable = c("Age >= 55", "Male", "Multifocal"),
  HR = c(1.85, 1.25, 1.08),
  P = c(0.0003, 0.012, 0.21)
)
pr_table(res, p_col = "P", highlight = 1)
#>   Variable      HR       P
#>   ────────────────────────
#>   Age >= 55   1.85  <0.001
#>   Male        1.25   0.012
#>   Multifocal  1.08   0.210
